method: Start from the reviewed Windows x64 selection. Every cargo package of the macOS graph that the Windows selection covers keeps its decision, selected license and texts; only role, features and platform-specific wording change.
Windows-only packages, the WebView2, MSVC and Windows runtime families, the NSIS/WiX installer families and their source archives are dropped.
Each macOS-only package has an explicit decision in scripts/release-license-select-macos.mjs; MIT is selected where offered, using the complete original text.

The standard-library mapping follows the installed aarch64/x86_64-apple-darwin rust-std RLIB names, std/Cargo.toml and library/Cargo.lock of the exact Rust commit. Outside windows-msvc, std carries the backtrace symbolization crates.
Frontend and npm decisions are reused unchanged: the same dist is bundled on both platforms.

reason.windows: Both dirs-sys versions unconditionally declare extern crate option_ext, so the dependency tree alone does not exclude it. Their only OptionExt use is user_dir.contains in xdg_user_dirs.rs, whose module is gated by unix and not macOS/iOS. The Windows implementation calls known-folder APIs instead. option-ext consists of a generic trait and generic impl only, with no initializer or non-generic runtime payload. Both existing release RLIBs contain a single 324-byte COFF object whose text/data/bss raw sizes are zero; metadata is not delivered as the application. No generic instantiation is claimed absent merely because the object is empty; the caller/cfg proof is necessary.
reason.macos: Both dirs-sys versions unconditionally declare extern crate option_ext, so the dependency tree alone does not exclude it. Their only OptionExt use is user_dir.contains in xdg_user_dirs.rs, whose module is gated by cfg(all(unix, not(any(target_os = "macos", target_os = "ios")))) and is therefore not compiled for either macOS target. option-ext consists of a generic trait and generic impl only, with no initializer or non-generic runtime payload. The Windows COFF size evidence is not repeated for macOS; the caller/cfg proof carries the decision.
